title.en: Charging and discharging of a capacitor

heading.en: Why does the charger LED fade slowly?

hook.en: Unplug some chargers and their LED glows for a second before fading out. A capacitor inside is discharging through a resistor, and the time it takes is set by R × C.
hook.kn: ಕೆಲವು ಚಾರ್ಜರ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ತೆಗೆದಾಗ LED ಒಂದು ಕ್ಷಣ ಉರಿದು ಆರುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಳಗಿನ ಧಾರಕ ರೋಧಕದ ಮೂಲಕ ವಿಸರ್ಜನೆಯಾಗುತ್ತಿದೆ; ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಬೇಕಾದ ಕಾಲ R × C.

objectives.en: Write the charging and discharging equations
Define the time constant τ = RC
Calculate capacitor voltage at a given time

narration.en: Unplug some chargers and their LED glows for a second before fading out. A capacitor inside is discharging through a resistor, and the time it takes is set by R × C.
narration.kn: ಕೆಲವು ಚಾರ್ಜರ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ತೆಗೆದಾಗ LED ಒಂದು ಕ್ಷಣ ಉರಿದು ಆರುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಳಗಿನ ಧಾರಕ ರೋಧಕದ ಮೂಲಕ ವಿಸರ್ಜನೆಯಾಗುತ್ತಿದೆ; ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಬೇಕಾದ ಕಾಲ R × C.

body.en: When a capacitor charges from a DC supply V through R, its voltage rises exponentially: $v_C = V(1 - e^{-t/RC})$, while the current falls: $i = (V/R) e^{-t/RC}$. The time constant $τ = RC$ is the time to reach 63.2 % of the final voltage. After about 5τ the capacitor is practically fully charged.
body.kn: R ಮೂಲಕ V ಆಕರದಿಂದ ಧಾರಕ ಆವೇಶಗೊಳ್ಳುವಾಗ ಅದರ ವಿಭವಾಂತರ ಘಾತೀಯವಾಗಿ ಏರುತ್ತದೆ, ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಇಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಕಾಲ ಸ್ಥಿರಾಂಕ τ = RC; ಅಷ್ಟು ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲಿ 63.2 % ತಲುಪುತ್ತದೆ. ಸುಮಾರು 5τ ನಲ್ಲಿ ಪೂರ್ಣ ಆವೇಶ.

title.en: On the board: Charging and discharging

say.en: Close the switch: the cell charges the capacitor through the resistor.
The capacitor voltage rises quickly at first, then more and more slowly. After one time constant, RC, it reaches 63.2 percent.
Discharging is the mirror image: the voltage falls to 36.8 percent after one time constant. After 5 RC it is practically complete.
These are the two equations, and the time constant is just R times C.
Example: 100 kilo-ohms and 10 microfarads give a time constant of 1 second; full charge in about 5 seconds.

body.en: A capacitor charged to V and discharged through R loses voltage exponentially: $v_C = V e^{-t/RC}$. After one time constant it falls to 36.8 % of V; after 5τ it is practically empty. The current flows in the opposite direction to the charging current.
body.kn: V ಗೆ ಆವೇಶಗೊಂಡ ಧಾರಕ R ಮೂಲಕ ವಿಸರ್ಜಿಸುವಾಗ vC = V e^(−t/RC). ಒಂದು τ ನಂತರ 36.8 % ಉಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ; 5τ ನಂತರ ಬಹುತೇಕ ಖಾಲಿ.

points.en: At t = τ: 36.8 % of V remains
Discharge current is opposite to charging current

problem.en: A 100 µF capacitor charges through 10 kΩ from a 10 V supply. Find τ and the voltage after 1 s.

steps.en: It is practically full (≈ 9.93 V) after 5 s.

problem.en: A 10 µF capacitor charged to 12 V discharges through 47 kΩ. Find τ and the voltage after one time constant.

body.en: In one time constant a charging capacitor gains 63 % of what is left to gain; a discharging one keeps 37 %. The two numbers always add to 100. Five time constants and you are done.
